newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iranian Kurds in Iraq hail German court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Iranian Kurds in Iraq hail German court ruling.

text.p: Iranian Kurds in Iraq on Tuesday said they were pleased by a German court verdict accusing Iran of ordering political killings of Kurdish dissidents.

"It has been a source of happiness to us although it cannot bring back to life our martyrs," Hassan Sharafi a senior member of Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran (KDPI) said in a news conference in Baghdad.

"We are so happy at the position taken by all the European countries. We hope such a position would force the Iranian regime to change its policy so that it cannot carry out such criminal acts inside and outside Iran," Sharafi said.
All European Union states except Greece have recalled ambassadors from Iran following the Berlin court verdict, although they have emphasised they do not want a break in relations.
Sharafi said three of the four Iranian Kurds killed in Germany were senior members of KDPI, including its secretary-general.
Sharafi held the news conference to draw attention to some 80 KDPI guerrillas being treated in Baghdad hospitals. He accused Tehran of contaminating their food with the toxic metal thallium.

The KDPI has camps in northern Iraq and Sharafi said the poisoning took place early this month at Bazyan, a makeshift camp of about 1,500 Iranian Kurds. His accusation could not be independently confirmed.
Sharafi said the patients were recovering quickly. The KDPI has good relations with the government in Baghdad, which fought a war with Iran from 1980 to 1988.
